title: [NSW] Dad & Dave’s Brewing – Selected 16 × 375mL cases $50 each + $15 shipping or free Brookvale pickup, until Black Friday
body:
Deal: [NSW] Dad & Dave’s Brewing – Selected 16 × 375mL cases $50 each + $15 shipping or free Brookvale pickup, until Black Friday

[Captain Yobbo] $50 for 16 x 3.5% beers seems like a pretty pissweek deal for some weak piss.
[dndbrewing] Thanks Yobbo! Plenty of other stronger ones on there
[ScottEh] Ok, and the 16 x 6.8% (if that's the UoM we're defining value on) beers for $50?
[Jason-z] I was going to order 4 cases but $60 delivery to WA killed it.
[dndbrewing] Unfortunately it's expensive to ship NSW to WA. Beers are already massively discounted
[opposablethumbs] Tend to agree, if you don't get any better shipping price for buying more than one case, then it's basically $65 per carton of 16, which is meh for a supposed sale.
Most other craft places I order from give flat or at least discounted shipping rates the more you buy.
[Jason-z] Agreed. I think $40 delivery would be reasonable but the craft beer industry is hit hard with ever increasing taxes, so I understand their need to charge delivery per case.
[TheDukeOfNukem] I have to ask, how did you come to 16?
Like, it's two thirds of a slab, and one more than half a case. How did you land on that number? Legitimately curious.
[dndbrewing] 16 can cases are common for craft beer. If we were doing 24's they'd be selling for $75 a case
[Captain Yobbo] It's a terrible example of shrinkflation, but you haven't explained WHY.
[TheDukeOfNukem] Okay…but why not sell a slab for 75 then?
Again, legit curious. Do you find more people buy when there's less in the box, or is price prohibitive? I feel like, much like cigarettes, the people who are going to spend, are going to do it anyway. I'm a numbers dude, I love knowing what goes into / comes out of sales and stuff like this.
[veritas_mendax] Pretty common for craft beer…Some of us don’t like to drink sh•t beer, and also want to support Aussie independent breweries at the same time
[TheDukeOfNukem] I haven't had a drink in around 5 years, but back when I did, I can't say I ever stumbled into a good craft beer…and about as many good craft beer drinkers.
But either way, at least the "shit beer" gives you a full slab.
In any case (heh, pun unintended), I still don't understand the breaking from the norm. 24 and 30 has been the go forever. 6/12 obviously also, but 16 is interesting. I could even see maybe it allows X amount more units to fit in shipping trucks for smaller scale businesses. But in any case, it being common, doesn't tell me why it's common. This isn't a trick or a trap or anything, I'm just curious what goes into it. It's obviously not done on a whim, so much goes into every business decision like this.
[werdplaya58] If I were to guess I would say manufacturing costs are typically higher for craft beers, so they are priced higher, and typically contain a higher ABV as well. So your average consumer might be more put off by the price if it were your standard 24 pack whereas 16 pack price point seems more like what they are used to, and mentally they put extra value on either the "craft" aspect, or the higher ABV, or both, to justify the lower quantity.
Obviously I'm not an expert and I'm sure manufacturers are able to squeeze a little more margin that way too, but ultimately it would not be a thing if there was not demand. It's also pretty much a norm in itself by now. So might as well just accept you've got 16, 24, or 30 packs, and usually very different beers in each, so it's not comapring apples with apples.
[werdplaya58] Are they close to code?
Why not list the BB dates?
[chickentaste] The number of smooth-brains who jump onto every craft beer deal just to feign surprise that 16 beers is (still) considered a case never fails to make me laugh.
[TheDukeOfNukem] Not surprised…but curious.
But do tell me why it's the case then. ;)
4x4 like the other dude makes sense…except…why did we drop from 6 packs as a standard down to 4? It's the same thing, why is there overall a third less provided? Shipping, partners, customer preference, I wanna know, goshdarnit.
[knuckle8] 16 beers and a bottle of Gin costs $30 for shipping to Melbourne.
Seems they need to sort out their shipping provider. Im sure you can push harder for better prices.
[the discombobulated…] Gah. So many things to try. The TIRAMISU Pastry Stout… how sweet is it? If it is…
